title: Nephi Makes His Record
summary: Nephi makes a record of his proceedings with his own hand.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi was born of goodly parents and taught somewhat in all the learning of his father.
Nephi saw many afflictions in the course of his days, yet was highly favored of the Lord in all his days.
Nephi had a great knowledge of the goodness and mysteries of God.
Nephi makes a record of his proceedings in his days.
Nephi makes the record in the language of his father, consisting of the learning of the Jews and the language of the Egyptians.
Nephi knows the record he makes is true, makes it with his own hand, and makes it according to his knowledge.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi is actively engaged in the physical act of engraving or writing his record with his own hand.
unspecified_visual_details: The physical medium of the record (such as metal plates, parchment, or tablets).
The specific tool or instrument Nephi uses to write.
Nephi's age, attire, facial features, and physical appearance.
The specific room, location, or environment where Nephi is writing.

narration.text: I, Nephi, having been born of goodly parents, therefore I was taught somewhat in all the learning of my father;
And I know that the record which I make is true; and I make it with mine own hand;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi establishes his identity, background, qualifications, and the truthfulness of his firsthand record at the opening of his account.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting Lehi or Sariah physically present in the scene, as they are only mentioned retrospectively.
Depicting specific afflictions or past visions not narrated as current events in these verses.
Specifying unmentioned writing tools or decorative motifs without basis in the text.

title: Prophets Warn Jerusalem
summary: In the commencement of the first year of the reign of Zedekiah, king of Judah, many prophets arrive among the people, prophesying that they must repent or the great city Jerusalem will be destroyed.

explicit_facts.text: It was the commencement of the first year of the reign of Zedekiah, king of Judah.
Lehi had dwelt at Jerusalem all his days.
In that same year, many prophets came and prophesied unto the people that they must repent, or the great city Jerusalem must be destroyed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The prophets are depicted speaking, gesturing, or addressing crowds in public streets or open gathering places of Jerusalem.
The people of Jerusalem are listening, passing by, or reacting to the warnings.
unspecified_visual_details: The specific number, names, ages, and attire of the prophets.
The architectural appearance of the streets, walls, or buildings of Jerusalem.
The specific emotional reactions, gestures, or makeup of the crowds.

narration.text: there came many prophets, prophesying unto the people that they must repent, or the great city Jerusalem must be destroyed.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Zedekiah is referenced strictly to establish the historical date and ruler, not as an active participant described in this scene.
Lehi's residence in Jerusalem is noted parenthetically by Nephi, but Lehi's specific action begins in verse 5.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting Zedekiah interacting with the prophets without textual basis.
Depicting the literal supernatural destruction of the city in this scene, as destruction is a warned consequence rather than an event taking place here.
Naming specific unnamed prophets (such as Jeremiah) not identified in the verse.

title: The Pillar of Fire
summary: Lehi goes forth and prays unto the Lord with all his heart in behalf of his people. While he prays, a pillar of fire comes and rests upon a rock before him, and he quakes and trembles exceedingly at what he sees and hears.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi went forth and prayed unto the Lord with all his heart in behalf of his people.
As Lehi prayed unto the Lord, a pillar of fire came and dwelt upon a rock before him.
Lehi saw and heard much, and because of what he saw and heard he did quake and tremble exceedingly.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi is outdoors in an open or rocky setting.
The pillar of fire casts a strong, dramatic light across Lehi and the surrounding terrain.
Lehi shows a posture of intense prayer, followed by visible shaking and trembling in response to the pillar of fire.
unspecified_visual_details: Lehi's exact age, facial features, and clothing style.
The precise dimensions, shape, and height of the pillar of fire.
The appearance, size, and type of the rock.
The time of day or night when the event takes place.

narration.text: there came a pillar of fire and dwelt upon a rock before him; and he saw and heard much; and because of the things which he saw and heard he did quake and tremble exceedingly.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The text states that Lehi saw and heard much, but the specific contents of what he saw and heard at the rock are not detailed in this passage.
The vision is given directly in response to Lehi praying with all his heart in behalf of his people.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting family members such as Nephi, Sariah, Laman, Lemuel, or Sam as witnesses to the event.
Showing specific heavenly personages within the pillar of fire that are not mentioned in the text.
Inventing specific audible dialogue or spoken words not recorded in these verses.

title: Lehi Rests upon His Bed
summary: Lehi returns to his house in Jerusalem and casts himself down upon his bed, overcome by the Spirit and the things he has seen.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi returned to his own house at Jerusalem.
He cast himself upon his bed.
He was overcome with the Spirit and the things which he had seen.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi is inside a private chamber or room of his home.
Lehi lies on a bed or sleeping mat in a state of physical exhaustion or profound emotional and spiritual overwhelm.
unspecified_visual_details: The architectural design, materials, and furnishings of Lehi's house.
The specific construction, framing, or textiles of the bed.
Lehi's exact posture, clothing, age appearance, and facial expression.

narration.text: he returned to his own house at Jerusalem; and he cast himself upon his bed, being overcome with the Spirit and the things which he had seen.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This occurs immediately after Lehi prayed concerning his people and experienced a manifestation of a pillar of fire upon a rock.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting family members such as Sariah, Nephi, Laman, Lemuel, or Sam in the room, as none are named or described in this verse.
Depicting visible floating spirits or supernatural fire inside the bedroom.
Inventing spoken dialogue or prayers not found in the text.

title: Vision of the Heavenly Host
summary: Lehi is carried away in vision and sees the heavens open. He sees God sitting on a throne surrounded by numberless concourses of singing and praising angels, followed by One descending whose luster exceeds the noonday sun, who is followed by twelve others shining brighter than stars.

explicit_facts.text: Being overcome with the Spirit, he was carried away in a vision and saw the heavens open.
He thought he saw God sitting upon his throne, surrounded with numberless concourses of angels in the attitude of singing and praising their God.
He saw One descending out of the midst of heaven whose luster was above that of the sun at noon-day.
He saw twelve others following him whose brightness exceeded that of the stars in the firmament.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi is seen looking upward into the open heavens while overcome by the Spirit.
The heavens appear parted or opened above.
God is seated elevated upon a throne amidst vast radiant crowds of praising angels.
The descending One emits an intense, brilliant white or golden light outshining daylight.
The twelve figures descending in trail shine brightly, resembling brilliant stars against the heavenly backdrop.
unspecified_visual_details: The material, ornamentation, or architectural form of the throne.
The specific facial features, hair, age, or clothing of God, the descending One, or the twelve others.
The immediate earthly location or posture of Lehi (e.g., standing, kneeling, or lying down).
The exact visual nature or formation of the angelic concourses.

narration.text: he thought he saw God sitting upon his throne, surrounded with numberless concourses of angels
he saw One descending out of the midst of heaven
And he also saw twelve others following him

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The vision occurs as a consequence of Lehi being overcome with the Spirit.
The verses do not explicitly identify the descending One by name, nor the twelve others, describing them strictly by their descent and brightness.
prohibited_inventions: Labeling or naming the One as Jesus Christ or the twelve as Apostles in dialogue or text, as names are not given in these verses.
Inventing dialogue, hymns, or spoken words for the angels, God, or the descending figures.
Depicting physical features like wings or halos not specified in the text.

title: Lehi Reads the Heavenly Book
summary: Heavenly figures come down to earth, and the first stands before Lehi, handing him a book and bidding him to read; as Lehi reads it, he is filled with the Spirit of the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: They came down and went forth upon the face of the earth.
The first came and stood before Lehi and gave him a book, bidding him to read.
As Lehi read, he was filled with the Spirit of the Lord.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi holds and looks down at the book to read it.
The first figure stands in close proximity facing Lehi.
The remaining figures disperse across the earthly setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The physical construction, material, and dimensions of the book.
The exact posture of Lehi (standing, kneeling, or sitting).
The visual manifestation of being filled with the Spirit.
The specific landscape or setting of the face of the earth.

narration.text: And they came down and went forth upon the face of the earth;
and the first came and stood before my father, and gave unto him a book, and bade him that he should read.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi identifies the recipient as 'my father', who is Lehi.
The verse indicates reading the book directly leads to being filled with the Spirit of the Lord.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting visible contents or text of the book before they are described in later verses.
Depicting Lehi speaking, crying out, or rejoicing (which occurs in later verses).
Adding invented dialogue beyond the text stating he was bidden to read.

title: Lehi Reads the Heavenly Book and Praises God
summary: Lehi reads from the book concerning Jerusalem's impending destruction and captivity in Babylon, and he exclaims aloud in praise of the Lord God Almighty.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi read concerning Jerusalem that it should be destroyed, its inhabitants should perish by the sword, and many should be carried away captive into Babylon.
Lehi said, "Wo, wo, unto Jerusalem, for I have seen thine abominations!"

After reading and seeing many great and marvelous things, Lehi exclaimed praises unto the Lord, declaring His works great and marvelous, His throne high in the heavens, and His power, goodness, and mercy over all inhabitants of the earth.
Lehi's soul rejoiced and his whole heart was filled because of the things the Lord had shown unto him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi is holding and looking upon the book or scroll as he reads and then exclaims.
Lehi displays deep emotion and reverence, looking up or gesturing in prayer and praise.
unspecified_visual_details: Lehi's physical surroundings and immediate setting.
The physical format, material, script, and appearance of the book.
Lehi's clothing, posture, and exact facial expressions.

spoken_dialogue.text: Great and marvelous are thy works, O Lord God Almighty!
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lehi

narration.text: for his soul did rejoice, and his whole heart was filled,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Lehi's exclamation affirms that the Lord will not suffer those who come unto Him to perish.
The events of Jerusalem's destruction and Babylonian captivity are read as prophecy, not witnessed as a physical battle occurring in this immediate scene.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting a present-tense battle scene of Jerusalem being destroyed or citizens being captured.
Showing God or angels visibly present without explicit textual narration of their appearance in these verses.
Adding other family members or onlookers who are not named or described in these verses.

title: Nephi Abridges His Father's Record on Plates
summary: Nephi makes an abridgment of his father's record upon plates that he made with his own hands, intending later to make an account of his own proceedings and life.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi does not make a full account of the things his father has written.
Nephi's father wrote many things which he saw in visions and in dreams, and many things which he prophesied and spoke to his children.
Nephi will make an account of his own proceedings in his days.
Nephi makes an abridgment of the record of his father upon plates made with his own hands.
After abridging the record of his father, Nephi will make an account of his own life.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi is shown engraving or preparing to engrave text onto metallic plates using a stylus or engraving tool.
Nephi may have his father's written record nearby for reference as he abridges it.
unspecified_visual_details: The physical appearance, dimensions, binding, and metal type of the plates.
The exact type, material, and design of the engraving instrument.
The specific indoor or outdoor setting where Nephi sits or stands to work on the plates.
Nephi's clothing, physical features, and age.

narration.text: And now I, Nephi, do not make a full account of the things which my father hath written,
Behold, I make an abridgment of the record of my father, upon plates which I have made with mine own hands;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The text explains the structural composition of Nephi's record: an abridgment of Lehi's extensive writings followed by Nephi's own account.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting Lehi physically present in the room dictating the record.
Depicting the dreams and visions of Lehi as literal supernatural visions occurring in the immediate scene.
Assuming the specific metal of the plates without textual identification in these verses.

title: Lehi Preaches in Jerusalem and the Jews Seek His Life
summary: Lehi goes forth among the people in Jerusalem to prophesy and testify of what he saw, heard, and read in the book regarding their wickedness, the coming of the Messiah, and the redemption of the world. The Jews mock him, become angry, and seek to take away his life.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi went forth among the people and began to prophesy and declare the things he had both seen and heard concerning the destruction of Jerusalem.
The Jews mocked Lehi because he testified of their wickedness and abominations.
Lehi testified that the things he saw, heard, and read in the book plainly manifested the coming of the Messiah and the redemption of the world.
When the Jews heard these things, they were angry with Lehi, as with the prophets of old whom they had cast out, stoned, and slain, and they sought his life to take it away.
Nephi states that the tender mercies of the Lord are over all those He has chosen because of their faith, to make them mighty unto deliverance.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi is depicted speaking earnestly or gesturing toward a gathering crowd of Jews in an open public space or street within Jerusalem.
The crowd displays mocking gestures, angry expressions, and threatening postures toward Lehi.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific architecture, streets, or public squares of Jerusalem.
Exact clothing, colors, and physical appearances of Lehi and the members of the crowd.
Specific weapons or items held by members of the crowd seeking Lehi's life.

narration.text: he went forth among the people, and began to prophesy and to declare unto them
And it came to pass that the Jews did mock him because of the things which he testified of them;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi is narrating retrospectively and is not explicitly stated to be physically present in this preaching scene.
The prophets of old who were stoned, cast out, and slain are mentioned as a historical comparison, not as physical figures in the present scene.
The Messiah, the Lord, and the destruction of Jerusalem are subjects of Lehi's preaching rather than present visible characters or events.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting actual stoning, physical assaults, or bloodshed taking place against Lehi.
Showing the physical personage of the Messiah appearing in the street.
Inventing named individuals among the mocking crowd.
